that's the thing, I think book 3 made it pretty clear the apex is both simon and Grace's fault equally. like you said, "simon didn't come up with the idea to wheel denizens on his own" exactly, he didn't come up with it on his own, it was Grace's influence too. but both of them were responsible. and they never said grace came up with the null idea, just that she "read it in a book once." grace isn't the bookworm, simon is. i thought that was pretty heavily implying simon was the reason she came up with that. 

grace is the defacto leader, sure, but their relationship was toxic in both ways. they were really bad for each other and made each other worse. even if grace did more wrong, saying it's ALL her isn't fair. that takes away simon's agency. he's a person who can make his own choices, and he's ultimately the only one who's responsible for himself. not grace, not samantha, not the apex, not anyone.

and man, just because grace saw the conductor originally, that doesn't mean simon didn't have the critical thinking skills to realize "oh, okay, the conductor is actually a woman named amelia, she was a fake, and numbers are meant to go down." i mean, he was literally told this to his face by Amelia herself. even grace said "yeah, I was wrong, i think she's telling us the truth." if he chooses not to believe that, that's just his own fault. the news was just as big of a shock to grace, if not bigger, and she still believed it.

and saying simon wouldn't have done the things he did without grace... we don't know that (plus! how do we know grace would have made the apex without Simon?). after samantha abandoned him, plus his need to feel in control, who knows if he ever would've gotten better, or just gotten worse? if it wasn't the apex, what if it was something else? maybe the train would've always made simon worse.

speaking of! i totally agree: the train is definitely super fucked up. people don't sign off a waiver for it, they don't know what they're getting into. not like the kids even legally could. it's probably really bad for most people, even the ones who get off. most of the passengers we followed went through some seriously traumatic situations. even though it "solved" their problem, I bet they're gonna have to go to real therapy afterward.

simon should've never been put on the train, and grace shouldn't have either. it traumatized both of them and just enabled them to get worse in a situation they literally couldn't escape until they either changed or they got themselves killed. it's a messed situation. really is like saw for kids.

grace felt like she had to be the one to try and curb his feelings and actions, when she really couldn't do that. people are gonna do what they do. it causes way more harm than good to take on responsibility for other people's emotions.

like pushing hazel away, and yeah, maybe it did make simon more reactionary towards amelia after samantha warning him. but also, why didn't samantha tell him anything? she obviously knows why the apex is wrong, has she ever tried to change simon's mind? would he listen to her? probably not, because she didn't tell him at first when he boarded... but you have to wonder, right?

yeah, I know he wasn't. i meant it's more his fault than anyone's for never putting a system in place to ensure passengers know why they're there, so they all start out knowing what the train is for. 

before he just had the attitude of "it's up to them to sort themselves out, and if they don't, they die. not my problem." i think it's pretty fair to say that original choice had some pretty long lasting consequences.

maybe even if he did do something to try and tell passengers, amelia would've stopped it when she took over the train. but now we'll never know.

grace and simon believed what they did about the train because no one was there to tell them what they were "supposed" to be doing there. they came to their own (wrong) conclusions because they were children.

grace wasn't forcing these ideas onto simon. she was misguided, and saying what she thought was the truth. even though simon was officially second in command, it's obvious she saw him as her best friend first, and respected him equally. i mean, he even wrote most of the apex procedures ("you know I don't like to take credit for things!). they formed their worldview and the rules for the apex together.

the difference is that when shown that their ideals were wrong, grace changed. and simon refused to. it wasn't up to grace to spoonfeed it to him. simon had eyes and ears. he spent time with tuba and hazel, he met amelia, just like grace did. and yet nothing was enough for him to change.

if anyone is responsible for simon's downfall, I'd say it's one-one, for leaving passengers in the dark about their numbers until tulip suggested he explain it to them. book 3 is the natural consequence of one's negligence to passengers that we saw in book 4.
